goal: Find drift between user-facing docs (README.md, docs/cli-reference.md) and the actual routing contract codified in skills/bakeoff-run/SKILL.md, in either direction.
background: Three files are in scope: README.md, docs/cli-reference.md, and skills/bakeoff-run/SKILL.md (all relative to the bakeoff/ plugin root).
skills/bakeoff-run/SKILL.md is the canonical routing/drafting contract that the /bakeoff:run skill executes at runtime.
README.md and docs/cli-reference.md are the user-facing surface that explains the same workflow.

Drift means: (a) a behavior the user-facing docs promise that SKILL.md does not enforce, OR (b) a contract rule SKILL.md enforces that the user-facing docs omit or describe incorrectly, OR (c) a claim that disagrees across the three files.
Each finding must cite both sides with file:line evidence. Single-file claims are out of scope.
Out of scope: style/wording/formatting issues without a behavioral mismatch, drift against code outside the three named files, and speculation without file:line evidence on both sides.

Categories of behavior most worth checking: flag routing and known-flag list, exit code semantics, approval verbs and preview shapes, single-vs-split-vs-multi-lens routing, escalation modes and recommendations, provider/judge defaults and the canonical pair, task-fit warnings, validation-warning handling, parallel-vs-sequential eligibility, and post-run continuation recommendations.

facet.focus: Identify concrete drift between README.md / docs/cli-reference.md and skills/bakeoff-run/SKILL.md - each finding must cite both sides with file:line evidence.
include: rules SKILL.md enforces that README or docs/cli-reference.md omit or contradict
behaviors README or docs/cli-reference.md promise that SKILL.md does not enforce
flag, mode, or routing claims that disagree between the three files
approval, preview, or exit-code semantics described inconsistently
provider, judge, or escalation defaults that differ across the files
exclude: style, wording, or formatting issues without a behavioral mismatch
speculation without file:line evidence on both sides
drift against code outside the three named files
